title: introduce-traffic-curvature-regression-detector-and-cutover-fuse
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context and motivation: Production canaries detect regressions by comparing pointwise metrics and smoothed baselines, but we repeatedly hit short-lived curvature events where latency/throughput trend shapes change (concave/convex inflections) and current detectors either over-react or under-signal. Those events led to two customer incidents last quarter where cutovers rolled back too late or prematurely throttled capacity. This PR adds a 'traffic curvature' regression detector that reasons about higher-order shape changes in latency and throughput time series, plus a new small runtime "cutover fuse" that ties curvature signals to staged rollback budgets.

What this PR does (high level): - Implements a curvature scoring module that computes second-derivative style signals across multiple time horizons (short/medium/long) with robust noise-tolerant smoothing. - Adds a composite detector that fuses curvature, percentile drift, and throughput slope into a single regression score with configurable thresholds per-tenant. - Introduces a Cutover Fuse runtime that applies a conservative pre-commit budget: when curvature indicates an accelerating degradation, flux is gated and the rollout pauses; if conservative amplification conditions persist the fuse decrements rollback budget and triggers an automated slow-rollback policy. - Adds telemetry, dashboards, and alert rules to visualize curvature heatmaps and the fuse state for every canary run. - New unit and integration tests, and a small canary simulator script to replay historical incidents and verify improved signal-to-noise.

Design notes: - Curvature is calculated as a weighted finite-difference across quantile buckets (50/90/95/99) to make the detector sensitive to tail inflections but robust to median jitter. - Multi-horizon aggregation uses exponential windowing (alpha tuned per-horizon) and a conservative bias term to avoid false positives during natural traffic ramps. - The Cutover Fuse is intentionally conservative: it requires sustained curvature amplification across two consecutive medium horizons or a medium+long corroboration before consuming rollback budget. - Config is exposed in the canary policy API (canary/policies/v1) with sensible defaults; ops can tune per-workload.

Checklist: - [x] Curvature scoring implementation (runtime/sentinel/curvature_detector.go) - [x] Composite detector and policy hooks (canary/detectors/curvature_fuse.go) - [x] Cutover Fuse runtime integration (orchestrator/fuse_controller.go) - [x] Telemetry and dashboards (observability/dashboards/curvature-overview.json) - [x] Canary simulator and historical replay (tools/canary-sim/replay_curvature.py) - [x] Unit + integration tests (tests/curvature/*)

Commits (summary): [commit 1] add curvature scoring primitives and tests; [commit 2] composite detector and API wiring; [commit 3] fuse controller and telemetry hooks; [commit 4] simulator and replay datasets; [commit 5] docs and dashboard assets; [commit 6] address review feedback and harden windows for noisy tenants.

Files changed (high level): - runtime/sentinel/curvature_detector.go (new) — implements curvature scoring and horizon aggregation; key exported function ScoreCurvature(timeSeries, options) returns per-quantile curvature metrics and confidence scores. - canary/detectors/curvature_fuse.go (new) — combines curvature with percentile drift and throughput slope into a single detection score and exposes threshold config. - orchestrator/fuse_controller.go (mod) — integrates fuse decision into rollout state machine; introduces RolloutBudget and FuseState. - observability/dashboards/curvature-overview.json (new) — Grafana dashboard panels for curvature heatmaps and fuse state. - tools/canary-sim/replay_curvature.py (new) — small utility to replay stored traces with injected curvature events. - tests/curvature/test_curvature_detector.py (new) — unit tests for scoring and threshold behavior. - canary/policies/defaults.yaml (mod) — default policy values for curvature thresholds and fuse budgets.

Review conversation (condensed): - Arjun: "Nice work on the multi-horizon design. Curious how this behaves under ramped traffic (e.g. planned marketing spikes). Can we avoid gating cutovers during scheduled ramps?" - Author (Maya): "Added a schedule-aware bypass in the fuse controller; it consults rollout windows and an optional external signal (traffic-shape hint) before consuming budget. See orchestrator/fuse_controller.go line 127 for the check." - Lina: "Telemetry looks good; can we add a panel showing false-positive incidence over time?" - Author: "Added an extra panel and a metric 'canary.curvature.false_positives' bumped in the detector when a signal is rolled back within 5 minutes without downstream regressions." - Elliot: "Test coverage is thin for mixed-signal cases (short curvature + long throughput slope). Add an integration test." - Author: "Added tests in tests/curvature/integration_mixed_signals.py and updated replay dataset to include mixed cases." - Arjun (approval): "LGTM after minor nits addressed." - Lina (approval): "Approved."

CI and verification: - Build: passed - Unit tests: passed (flaky-db-connector retried once) - Integration tests: passed - Lint: passed - Security scan: passed with low-severity findings (dependency click upgrade recommended). All checks GREEN at merge.

Risk and rollout plan: - Default policy is disabled for all production tenants; rollout to canary experiments only. - Step 1: enable on internal canaries (2 weeks) to measure false positive rate. - Step 2: enable on non-critical customer namespaces with telemetry-only mode (no fuse consumption) for 4 weeks. - Step 3: enable conservative fuse budget for high-sensitivity tenants and monitor. - Ops contact: @oncall-canary for immediate rollbacks.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-1428 tracks prior incidents; SUP-9021 contains customer repro traces. Also builds on prior percentile drift detectors (see pr-321456 and pr-412678). This PR aims to complement existing detectors rather than replace them.

release_notes: Introduces a curvature-based regression detector and a conservative cutover fuse to reduce mis-handled inflection-driven regressions. Disabled by default; must be enabled via canary policy. Includes dashboards and simulator for validation.
notes_for_ops: Default off for prod. Use observability/dashboards/curvature-overview.json to inspect signals. Contact oncall for debug. Policy knobs: curvature.horizon.short.alpha, curvature.horizon.medium.alpha, fuse.rollback_budget.
